newsitem.title: USA: Procter & Gamble fourth quarter, year higher.
newsitem.headline: Procter & Gamble fourth quarter, year higher.

text.p: Consumer products giant Procter & Gamble Co. said Thursday that stronger sales and unit volume growth led to higher earnings for the fourth quarter and full year.

"We have had another very strong quarter of earnings and cash flow growth," Chief Executive John Pepper said. "I am also particularly pleased with the acceleration in fourth-quarter net sales and unit volume growth."
For the fourth quarter, P&G earned $611 million, or 87 cents per share, compared with $554 million, or 77 cents per share, a year earlier. Sales rose to $8.95 billion from $8.58 billion.
The company, based in Cincinnati, said the higher per share growth reflects fewer shares outstanding.
P&G's major product lines include Tide, Ariel, Pantene Pro-V, Always, Whisper, Pringles, Pampers and Oil of Olay.
Worldwide net sales for the year were $35.8 billion, up 1 percent from $35.3 billion, on unit volume growth of 3 percent.
The difference between sales and volume growth rates reflects weaker currencies in Europe and Asia, the company said.
Earnings for the year rose to $3.41 billion, or $4.87 a share, from $3.0 billion, or $4.29 a share, a year earlier.

The company said its North America region continued to deliver solid progress, achieving record sales, unit volume and earnings. Sales were $17.70 billion, an increase of 2 percent on unit volume growth of 4 percent.

The difference between sales and unit volume growth was primarily due to product mix, lower pricing in laundry products and lower commodity-based paper pricing, P&G said. Excluding the 1996 gain on the sale of its health care joint venture stake, North America earnings rose 8 percent to $2.30 billion.

Laundry detergents and fabric conditioners continued to drive the region's unit volume progress. The Food and Beverage sector, aided by new snacks production capacity, and the Paper sector also contributed to the volume gain.

P&G said Europe, Middle East, and Africa unit volume grew 7 percent for the year, generating about one-half of the company's total volume growth. Sales grew 1 percent to $11.58 billion. The difference between sales and unit volume growth primarily reflects unfavourable exchange rates and lower commodity-based paper pricing.

The region's earnings grew 20 percent to $857 million, driven by volume growth and cost control, generated through simplification and standardisation efforts. Central and Eastern Europe and the Middle East and Africa led the region's unit volume growth.
Results in Asia were mixed, P&G said. The region had a 7 percent decline in unit volume for the year. Sales were down 8 percent to $3.57 billion.

Improved pricing and product mix were offset by the impact of unfavourable exchange rate movements. Weak unit volume reflected softness in Japan, which was partially offset by double digit volume growth in the Philippines and Indonesia.
The region's earnings were $274 million, an 8 percent increase over 1996, and reflected simplification and standardisation efforts and the divestiture of non-strategic brands.

Unit volume for the Latin America region was down 2 percent, as the region continues to be affected by economic difficulties and a slower than anticipated recovery in consumption levels, P&G said. However, sales in the region grew 6 percent to $2.30 billion as inflation-driven pricing action more than offset the effects of lower volume. Earnings for the region were $217 million, a 4 percent increase.
Procter & Gamble's stock was down 93.75 cents to $152.06 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
